— Conrad's personal motto.[[3]](#cite_note-NYT-3)

While at Princeton, Conrad met Jane DuBose, a student at [Bryn Mawr](/wiki/Bryn_Mawr_College "Bryn Mawr College"), whose family owned a 1,600-acre (650 ha) ranch near [Uvalde, Texas](/wiki/Uvalde,_Texas "Uvalde, Texas"). Her father, Winn DuBose, was the first person to call Conrad "Pete" rather than "Peter", the name he had used since birth. Upon his graduation from Princeton and acceptance of his navy commission, Conrad and Jane were married on June 16, 1953. They had four sons.[[2]](#cite_note-rocketman-2)

Given the demands of his career in the Navy and NASA, Conrad and Jane spent considerable time apart, and Conrad saw less of his sons than he would have liked. In 1988, Conrad and Jane divorced, both later remarrying.[[9]](#cite_note-nasabio-9)[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26)

In 1989, Conrad's youngest son, Christopher, was diagnosed with a malignant [lymphoma](/wiki/Lymphoma "Lymphoma"). He died in April 1990, at the age of 29.[[2]](#cite_note-rocketman-2): 230–1

Conrad met [Nancy Crane](/wiki/Nancy_Conrad "Nancy Conrad"), a [Denver](/wiki/Denver,_Colorado "Denver, Colorado") divorcee, through mutual friends. Conrad and Crane married in 1990.[[27]](#cite_note-27)

Conrad was a [Cub Scout](/wiki/Cub_Scouting_(Boy_Scouts_of_America) "Cub Scouting (Boy Scouts of America)").[[28]](#cite_note-28) His recreational interests included [golf](/wiki/Golf "Golf"), [water skiing](/wiki/Water_skiing "Water skiing") and [auto racing](/wiki/Auto_racing "Auto racing"), such as [Formula Vee](/wiki/Formula_Vee "Formula Vee").[[29]](#cite_note-29)

In the late 19th century, a literary movement called *[verismo](/wiki/Verismo_(literature) "Verismo (literature)")*, which extolled realism, played a major role in Italian literature. [Emilio Salgari](/wiki/Emilio_Salgari "Emilio Salgari"), a writer of action-adventure [swashbucklers](/wiki/Swashbuckler "Swashbuckler") and a pioneer of science fiction, published his *[Sandokan](/wiki/Sandokan "Sandokan")* series.[[342]](#cite_note-348) In 1883, [Carlo Collodi](/wiki/Carlo_Collodi "Carlo Collodi") published *[The Adventures of Pinocchio](/wiki/The_Adventures_of_Pinocchio "The Adventures of Pinocchio")*, which became the most celebrated children's classic by an Italian author and one of the world's [most translated](/wiki/List_of_literary_works_by_number_of_translations "List of literary works by number of translations") non-religious books.[[343]](#cite_note-349) A movement called [futurism](/wiki/Futurism "Futurism") influenced literature in the early 20th century. [Filippo Tommaso Marinetti](/wiki/Filippo_Tommaso_Marinetti "Filippo Tommaso Marinetti") wrote *[Manifesto of Futurism](/wiki/Manifesto_of_Futurism "Manifesto of Futurism")* and called for the use of language and metaphors that glorified the speed, dynamism, and violence of the machine age.[[344]](#cite_note-350)

Modern literary figures are [Gabriele D'Annunzio](/wiki/Gabriele_D%27Annunzio "Gabriele D'Annunzio"), nationalist poet [Giosuè Carducci](/wiki/Giosu%C3%A8_Carducci "Giosuè Carducci") 1906 Nobel laureate, realist writer [Grazia Deledda](/wiki/Grazia_Deledda "Grazia Deledda") 1926 laureate, modern theatre author [Luigi Pirandello](/wiki/Luigi_Pirandello "Luigi Pirandello") in 1936, short story writer [Italo Calvino](/wiki/Italo_Calvino "Italo Calvino") in 1960, poets [Salvatore Quasimodo](/wiki/Salvatore_Quasimodo "Salvatore Quasimodo") in 1959 and [Eugenio Montale](/wiki/Eugenio_Montale "Eugenio Montale") in 1975, [Umberto Eco](/wiki/Umberto_Eco "Umberto Eco") in 1980, and satirist and theatre author [Dario Fo](/wiki/Dario_Fo "Dario Fo") in 1997.[[345]](#cite_note-351)

The [Scandinavian Mountains](/wiki/Scandinavian_Mountains "Scandinavian Mountains") are the most defining feature of the country. Starting with [Setesdalsheiene](/wiki/Setesdalsheiene "Setesdalsheiene") north of the [Skagerrak](/wiki/Skagerrak "Skagerrak") coast, the mountains are found in large parts of the country and intersect the many fjords of [Vestlandet](/wiki/Vestlandet "Vestlandet"). This region includes [Hardangervidda](/wiki/Hardangervidda "Hardangervidda"), [Jotunheimen](/wiki/Jotunheimen "Jotunheimen") (with [Galdhøpiggen](/wiki/Galdh%C3%B8piggen "Galdhøpiggen") at 2,469 metres (8,100 ft) [a.s.l.](/wiki/Metres_above_sea_level "Metres above sea level")), [Sognefjell](/wiki/Sognefjell "Sognefjell"), and [Trollheimen](/wiki/Trollheimen "Trollheimen") in the north, with large glaciers, such as [Jostedalsbreen](/wiki/Jostedalsbreen "Jostedalsbreen"), [Folgefonna](/wiki/Folgefonna "Folgefonna"), and [Hardangerjøkulen](/wiki/Hardangerj%C3%B8kulen "Hardangerjøkulen"). The mountain chain swings eastwards south of Trondheim, with ranges such as [Dovrefjell](/wiki/Dovrefjell "Dovrefjell") and [Rondane](/wiki/Rondane "Rondane"), and reaches the border with Sweden, where they have become mostly gently sloping plateaus. The mountains then follow the border in a northeasterly direction and are known as *Kjølen* (the "keel"). The mountains intersect many fjords in [Nordland](/wiki/Nordland "Nordland") and [Troms](/wiki/Troms "Troms"), where they become more alpine and create many islands after they meet the sea. The Scandinavian mountains form the [Lyngen Alps](/wiki/Lyngen_Alps "Lyngen Alps"), which reach into northwestern [Finnmark](/wiki/Finnmark "Finnmark"), gradually becoming lower from [Altafjord](/wiki/Altafjord "Altafjord") towards the [North Cape](/wiki/North_Cape_(Norway) "North Cape (Norway)"), where they finally end at the [Barents Sea](/wiki/Barents_Sea "Barents Sea").

In 1896, the **Nanyang Public School** (南洋公学) was founded in [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") based on an imperial edict issued by the [Guangxu Emperor](/wiki/Guangxu_Emperor "Guangxu Emperor"), under the Business and Telegraphs Office of the [imperial government](/wiki/Qing_dynasty "Qing dynasty"). Four schools were established: a [normal school](/wiki/Normal_school "Normal school"), a school of foreign studies, a middle school, and a [high school](/wiki/Nanyang_Model_High_School "Nanyang Model High School"). [Sheng Xuanhuai](/wiki/Sheng_Xuanhuai "Sheng Xuanhuai"), the mandarin who proposed the idea to the Guangxu Emperor, became the first president and is regarded as the founder of the university, along with [John Calvin Ferguson](/wiki/John_Calvin_Ferguson "John Calvin Ferguson"), a missionary educator.

The university underwent a series of transitions. In 1904, the Ministry of Commerce took over the school, and in 1905 changed its name to **Imperial Polytechnic College of the Commerce Ministry**. In 1906, the college was placed under the Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs, and its name was changed to **Shanghai Industrial College of the Ministry of Posts and Telegraphs**. When the [Republic of China](/wiki/Republic_of_China_(1912%E2%80%931949) "Republic of China (1912–1949)") was founded, the college was placed under the Ministry of Communications and its name was once again changed, this time to **Government Institute of Technology of the Communications Ministry**
